learning_objective: 🎯 Master the theoretical framework (Arohav, Avaroh, Vadi, Samvadi, Pakad) of prescribed Ragas and understand how Bandishes (compositions) are structured within them.

key_vocabulary.definition: The most important or 'King' note of a Raga, played most frequently.
The second most important or 'Minister' note of a Raga.
A signature catch-phrase of notes that instantly identifies a Raga.
The remaining 'citizen' notes used in the Raga (neither Vadi nor Samvadi).
An 'enemy' or forbidden note, occasionally used by masters for a fleeting aesthetic effect.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The morning raga. Thaat: Bhairav. Jati: Sampoorna-Sampoorna (7 notes up, 7 down). Vadi: Dha, Samvadi: Re. Special feature: Rishabh (Re) and Dhaivat (Dha) are Komal (flat), while all other notes are Shuddha. It evokes a mood of devotion and peace (Bhakti and Shanti Rasa).

The midnight raga. Thaat: Kafi. Jati: Audav-Sampoorna (5 up, 7 down; Re and Pa are omitted in Arohav). Vadi: Ma, Samvadi: Sa. Special feature: Gandhar (Ga) and Nishad (Ni) are Komal. It evokes a mood of romance and yearning (Shringar Rasa).

A serious midnight raga. Thaat: Bhairavi. Jati: Audav-Audav (5 up, 5 down; Re and Pa are strictly omitted). Vadi: Ma, Samvadi: Sa. Special feature: Ga, Dha, and Ni are Komal. It creates a deep, meditative, and majestic atmosphere.

A Bandish (composition) has two main parts: the 'Sthayi' (the first half, usually revolving around the lower and middle octaves, Sa to Pa) and the 'Antara' (the second half, revolving around the upper middle and high octaves, Ma to Taar Sa).

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Find the Missing Notes
fun_activity.instructions: Raga Malkauns uses 5 notes: Sa, Komal Ga, Shuddha Ma, Komal Dha, and Komal Ni. Which two notes are completely missing? (Answer: Re and Pa). Because 'Pa' (the fifth) is missing, instruments accompanying Malkauns must tune their first string to 'Ma' instead of 'Pa'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always format Raga descriptions with clear headings: Thaat, Jati, Swaras (Komal/Teevra), Vadi, Samvadi, Time of Singing, and Pakad.
📌 The Vadi and Samvadi are usually separated by a distance of 3 or 4 notes (a 4th or 5th interval).
📌 Remember: Raga Bhairav is sung in the morning (Sandhiprakash), while Bageshri and Malkauns are sung at midnight.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Pakad' acts like the ID card of a Raga, separating it from other Ragas of the same Thaat.
⭐ Forbidden notes (Varjit Swaras) must never be sung, as they will destroy the purity of the Raga.
⭐ The combination of Vadi and time of day is deeply connected (e.g., Bhairav's Vadi 'Dha' is in the Uttarang, making it a morning raga).
